explanation.summary: Show the forecast recipes that earned the top grade, all 63 of them, each with its recipe in plain words and the numbers it earned them with.

verdicts: Pointed the other way in the held-back years
Too little held-back data to judge

grading_rule: A recipe earned the top grade only if all of this held. It was one of the 1,217 recipes the first search promoted. The second search could test it again (enough days and enough stocks). It pointed the same way in the second search as in the first. And in the second search it passed every one of that search's own gates again: a screen that limits false alarms when thousands of recipes are tested at once, a check that it pointed the same way in stretch after stretch of the earlier years, a check on the held-back later years it had not been picked on, a check that it still worked after trading costs, and a check that enough money could actually trade it. Anything weaker earned a lower grade, not this one.

groups.title: Unusually busy trading: forecasting how much a stock moves, next 20 trading days
groups.watches: Where today's trading activity sits in the stock's own recent past. Activity is the stock's price times its shares traded, logged; the reading is that figure's rank within the stock's own last 252 trading days, from 0 (the quietest) to 1 (the busiest). A higher reading means an unusually busy stock.

groups.expects: Stocks with a higher reading will in fact move around more over the next 20 trading days.
groups.title: A jumpiness formula: forecasting how much a stock moves, next 20 trading days
groups.watches: A fixed formula that forecasts how much a stock's price will move around. Each day it blends three parts: 90% of yesterday's forecast, 8% of that day's squared move, and 2% of the stock's long-run average restlessness (its average over the last 252 trading days). A higher reading means the formula expects a jumpier stock.

cells.where: Counted across every stock and every day, with no narrowing.
Counted only on days when SPY closed above its average price of the last 200 trading days and that average was higher than it was 20 trading days earlier.

groups.expects: The lower the reading, the more SPY will move around over the next 5 trading days.
groups.title: Dealer gamma rank: forecasting how much SPY moves, next 5 trading days
groups.watches: Where the whole market's dealer gamma reading sits in its own recent past. The reading tracks how much dealers, as a group, would have to buy or sell as prices move; this cell uses its rank within the last 252 trading days. This recipe runs the other way from the others: a lower reading goes with a jumpier market.

overlap_note: One limit travels with the top grade, in the second search's own words: its second set of stocks covers the same calendar years as the first search's held-back years. So the top grade means a recipe held up on a separately gathered set of stocks, a different mix of companies, and a fresh split of the same years. It does not mean the recipe has been tested in new years; only time going forward can test that.
proving_words: The tool's numbers are the counted result of a study that has already run on the record.
